explanations: terra: Patience and prayer are commanded as means of help, yet prayer is called difficult except for the humble; a divinely given means of ease can itself feel heavy to its practitioner.
terra: Believers are told to seek help through patience and prayer because إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ; divine company is located within endurance of difficulty.
terra: The regulated remission in retaliation is called a lightening from the Lord and mercy, a concrete legal reduction of burden parallel to the fasting concession.

luna: This preceding fasting ayah gives the sick and traveler a way to make up the fast later. The section names those exemptions as the immediate setting for 2:185's declaration that God wants ease. | terra: The sick and traveler may complete the fast on other days and a feeding substitute is named; these concrete accommodations are the basis for 2:185's declaration that God intends ease.

luna: After fasting exemptions for the sick and traveler, this ayah explicitly says God intends ٱلْيُسْرَ and does not intend ٱلْعُسْرَ. It names both sides of the section's pairing, here as the law's guiding preference. | terra: God says He intends الْيُسْرَ and does not intend الْعُسْرَ in the fasting concession, making divine accommodation a direct form of the section's paired terms.

luna: This describes believers being struck by adversity and shaken until they ask when God's help will come, then answers that God's help is near. It is a concrete communal scene of hardship with relief promised within it. | terra: After believers are shaken until the messenger asks when help will come, أَلَا إِنَّ نَصْرَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ places relief at the extremity of hardship.
terra: In regulating care for orphans, the ayah says that had God willed He could have made matters difficult for the believers; the unrealized hardship clarifies divine accommodation in social law.

terra: In the same nursing scene as 65:6, no mother or father may be harmed through the child, support follows recognized means, and weaning is by mutual consultation; it shows ease practiced between people.

luna: For a debtor in hardship (عُسْرَةٍ), the creditor is told to wait until easier circumstances (مَيْسَرَةٍ), or forgive the debt. This same-root pairing makes relief a later respite, contrasting with the section's ease alongside hardship. | terra: عُسْرَةٍ ... مَيْسَرَةٍ stages a debtor in straits and commands respite until ease; it concretizes both the antonym pair and the source dictionary's act of showing ease to another.

luna: The ayah bounds what is asked of a soul by what it can bear (وُسْعَهَا), then prays not to be loaded with an unbearable burden (إِصْرًا). The section's image of a weight removed meets this boundary on hardship. | terra: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا gives capacity as the boundary of burden and ends with prayers not to be loaded beyond strength.
terra: God reminds the believers that He helped them at Badr while they were weak, an explicit statement of aid present within acknowledged vulnerability.
terra: The Prophet's gentleness keeps people near, while harshness and hard-heartedness would scatter them; pardon and consultation enact the source dictionary's ease toward another.

luna: In its marriage rulings, this says God wants to lighten things for people (يُخَفِّفَ عَنكُمْ) because humanity is weak. That gives a concrete Quranic counterpart to the section's dictionary sense of ease as lightness. | terra: يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنكُمْ states God's will to lighten the human burden because the human being was created weak, a nonlexical formulation of intended ease.
terra: Casting the aggressive wrongdoer into fire is وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا; “easy for God” plainly does not mean slight in consequence.
terra: Everlasting passage into hell is وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا, again separating divine ease of enactment from moral or experiential lightness.

luna: In the purification ruling, the ayah allows dry ablution in cases such as travel or illness and says God does not intend hardship (حَرَجٍ). It is a specific legal ease in bodily difficulty, parallel to the section's fasting example. | terra: After ablution and its dry substitute, مَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْ حَرَجٍ denies that the law aims to impose constriction and instead names purification and completed favor.

terra: بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ joins the dual-hand image to unrestricted giving; it may illuminate the source's two hands working together, though its main contrast is with the false claim of a fettered divine hand.

luna: The section invokes the Prophet's chest being opened as evidence of ease; this ayah contrasts an opened breast with a tight, constricted one (ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا) for the person who rejects guidance. It gives the bodily opposite of that opening. | terra: God expands the breast of the guided but makes the breast of the one led astray ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا, a bodily contrast that illuminates opened breast as ease within the section.
terra: Amid commands about orphan property, measure, and truthful speech, God says He charges no soul beyond its capacity, extending the section's burden-and-ease relation into daily justice.
terra: God's straight path is singular while the other ways split people away from it, an explicit path boundary for the section's one prepared way and resistant deviation.
terra: The righteous are promised the garden with the reminder that God charges no soul beyond its capacity, joining bounded burden to the easy outcome of salvation.

luna: The Prophet's mission is described as lifting the followers' burden and shackles (إِصْرَهُمْ وَالْأَغْلَالَ). This directly parallels the section's load being taken off as evidence that ease is present within the trial. | terra: The Messenger يَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَالْأَغْلَالَ removes burdens and shackles; it is a communal parallel to the load taken from the Prophet before 94:5.
terra: In battle the believers seek rescue and God answers with promised angelic reinforcement, placing responsive aid inside the moment of military distress.
terra: The reinforcement is made good news so that hearts may become tranquil, while victory belongs only to God; inner ease arrives before the danger has ended.
terra: Drowsiness gives security and rain purifies, removes Satan's defilement, strengthens hearts, and firms feet, a cluster of simultaneous eases within the battlefield's hardship.

terra: Dispute would make the believers falter and lose strength, while patience carries the promise إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ; entangling opposition and sustaining company are placed side by side.

luna: After the preceding command to fight, this says God has lightened the burden (خَفَّفَ عَنكُمْ), knowing the believers' weakness. It is a specific easing of a strenuous duty and echoes the section's secondary sense of ease as lightness.

luna: In the call to march, the ayah says they cling heavily to the earth (اثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ). The section's dictionary note gives ease a sense of lightness, and 9:117 names the same campaign's hour of hardship; this makes reluctance's weight a concrete counterimage.
terra: In the cave, the Prophet says لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا before tranquility and unseen aid descend; divine ease is present “with” danger rather than waiting for danger to vanish.

luna: The mobilization command is to go forth light and heavy (خِفَافًا وَثِقَالًا) and strive with wealth and lives. The section's dictionary note glosses ease as light, while 9:117 calls this campaign an hour of hardship, bringing physical readiness and strenuous service together.

luna: The same campaign scene says they would have followed for an easy gain and short journey (عَرَضًا قَرِيبًا وَسَفَرًا قَاصِدًا), but the distance was hard for them. This gives the easy-versus-difficult route a concrete mobilization setting beside 9:117. | terra: The hypocrites would have followed for nearby gain and a moderate journey, but the arduous distance deterred them; it exposes attraction to what is merely easy while refusing a difficult faithful task.

luna: In the campaign context, the weak, sick, and those without means to contribute are excused from blame. This is a specific easing of a difficult obligation in the same surah that later recalls the hour of hardship.

luna: This recalls the Prophet and the believers who followed him in the hour of hardship (سَاعَةِ الْعُسْرَةِ), then says God turned toward them. It gives the section's hardship-root a historical scene of strain met by divine mercy. | terra: سَاعَةِ الْعُسْرَةِ names the concrete hour of the Tabuk expedition in which divine turning and mercy accompanied the Prophet and his followers.

luna: The next ayah describes the three who stayed behind: the earth felt constricted despite its vastness, and they felt constricted in themselves, before God turned to them. It continues the hardship-hour scene in 9:117 with a specific crisis followed by relief. | terra: After 9:117's hour of hardship, the earth becomes narrow despite its vastness and the three men's souls constrict before God turns to them, showing inner and outer constriction opening into mercy.

luna: This describes good fortune coming after affliction (نَعْمَاءَ بَعْدَ ضَرَّاءَ) and the person's claim that hardship has gone. It offers a specific sequential framing of relief, illuminating the section's emphasis on ease accompanying hardship.
terra: Jacob commands his sons to search and not despair مِن رَّوْحِ اللَّهِ; expected divine relief remains available while Joseph and his brother are still absent.
terra: When messengers reach the point of despair and think themselves denied, جَاءَهُمْ نَصْرُنَا; it stages help at the tightest point of difficulty.

luna: The section links ease to the Quran being made accessible for remembrance; this ayah says hearts find rest through remembrance of God (بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ). It develops what remembrance can bring beyond access to recitation.
terra: Every messenger is sent in his people's language لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ; intelligible language supplies the communicative purpose behind the Quran being eased on the Prophet's tongue.
terra: قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ is set against paths that are جَائِرٌ; directed and deviating ways provide a Quranic path image for ease as straight readiness versus difficulty as bending away.
terra: Against the charge that a human teaches the Prophet, the ayah contrasts a foreign tongue with this clear Arabic tongue, clarifying the public intelligibility involved in linguistic ease.
terra: The Quran guides لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ, joining the eased revelation to the most upright course it opens for its hearers.

luna: When a person cannot give needy relatives what they ask for, the ayah still requires a gentle word (قَوْلًا مَيْسُورًا). The section's dictionary form ياسره means to treat someone leniently; this is that interpersonal easing in a specific scene. | terra: قَوْلًا مَيْسُورًا requires an accessible, gentle word when one cannot yet give to needy relatives and travelers, concretizing the dictionary sense “show ease to him.”

luna: In the counsel about responding to needy relatives, this warns against keeping a hand bound to the neck or extending it without limit. The section joins ease shown to others with the giver's path and the miser's opposite path; this ayah places giving and withholding in a concrete hand image.
terra: The Book is sent down with no عِوَجًا; its absence of crookedness directly joins revelation to the source's contrast between tangled resistance and prepared ease.
terra: قَيِّمًا continues 18:1 by presenting the Book as upright so that it can warn and give believers good news, the operative consequence of its uncrooked form.
terra: The youths ask هَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا; هَيِّئْ is the very “prepare” wording used in the source dictionary to explain how ease comes about amid their danger.

luna: The youths flee persecution and seek refuge in a cave, asking God to spread mercy and prepare for them a comfort (مَرْفِقًا). The section's dictionary note glosses ease as something made ready; this is a specific provision prepared within distress. | terra: وَيُهَيِّئْ لَكُم مِّنْ أَمْرِكُم مِّرْفَقًا answers the cave scene with prepared relief, making a place of refuge and facility available inside persecution.

luna: After forgetting his promise to Khidr, Moses asks not to be burdened with difficulty in his affair (عُسْرًا). The section's hardship-root is used in a concrete plea for relief amid a difficult undertaking. | terra: Moses asks his companion not to load his affair with عُسْرًا after forgetting his pledge, staging difficulty as an added burden in a shared task.

luna: After promising the good-doer the best reward, Dhu al-Qarnayn says he will speak to him from his command with ease (يُسْرًا). The section's dictionary form ياسره means to deal leniently with someone; this is an interpersonal rather than path-making use of that easing. | terra: سَنَقُولُ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًا promises the righteous subject of Dhu al-Qarnayn an easy or gentle command, pairing just rule with ease toward another.
terra: هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ uses هَيِّن, the source dictionary's gloss for يَسِير, for God's creation of John despite humanly impossible conditions.
terra: هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ repeats the same dictionary synonym in Mary's harder-seeming case and grounds ease in divine power rather than ordinary conditions.
terra: God grants Abraham and his family mercy and makes for them a lofty truthful mention, a direct parallel to divine relief accompanied by raised remembrance.

luna: God says He made the Quran easy in the Prophet's tongue (يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكَ) so he may bring good news and warn. This directly develops the section's claim that the Quran is facilitated through the Prophet's speech. | terra: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكَ locates the Quran's ease on the Prophet's tongue so that it can give good news and warning.

luna: At the start of the address to Moses' namesake, this says the Quran was not sent down to make the Prophet distressed (لِتَشْقَىٰ), but as a reminder. That specifically complements the section's Quran made easy for remembrance. | terra: مَا أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقَىٰ denies that revelation was sent to make the Prophet wretched, setting a clear boundary around the section's Quran-made-easy claim.
terra: إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ supplies remembrance for the one who fears as revelation's purpose, joining the remembrance formulas of 54 with the fearing recipient of 87 and 92.

luna: Before Moses asks in 20:26 for his affair to be made easy, he asks God to expand his chest. This reprises the opened-chest image that the section treats as evidence of ease arriving within difficulty. | terra: رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي immediately precedes Moses' request for ease in 20:26 and joins opened breast to an eased task exactly as the section joins 94:1 to 94:5.

luna: Before his mission to Pharaoh, Moses asks God to make his affair easy (وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي). It is a direct plea for ease within a daunting task. | terra: Moses asks وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي; ease is something God makes ready inside the very commission that occasions fear and burden.

luna: In the same plea as 20:26, Moses asks God to untie a knot in his tongue (عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِي). The section's dictionary gloss for hardship includes twisting and entanglement, so this is a concrete speech-knot beside his request for ease. | terra: وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِي turns the source dictionary's tangled, knotted difficulty into a literal knot whose loosening prepares speech.

luna: Moses asks that people understand his speech (يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي), the result sought by the knot-removal in 20:27. This develops the section's claim about speech being made easy through a prophet's tongue. | terra: يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي states what the loosening in 20:27 makes possible: an eased tongue becomes intelligible speech.
terra: وَاجْعَل لِّي وَزِيرًا مِّنْ أَهْلِي asks for a helper as part of Moses' answer to a difficult commission; the helper will make the single task shared.
terra: هَارُونَ أَخِي identifies the companion who will supply the second worker in the shared labor developed through 20:32.
terra: اشْدُدْ بِهِ أَزْرِي asks that Aaron strengthen Moses' back, reversing the load that breaks the back in the surrounding surah 94 image.
terra: وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِي أَمْرِي asks that Aaron share Moses' task, a narrative counterpart to the section's two hands working together in one labor.
terra: كَيْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيرًا gives the purpose of the eased and shared task: abundant glorification.
terra: وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيرًا completes the purpose of Moses' requested ease with abundant remembrance, linking eased work and dhikr.
terra: اذْهَبَا إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ sends the two together into the feared task, the setting in which 20:44 requires gentleness and 20:46 promises divine company.

terra: فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَّيِّنًا commands Moses and Aaron to use gentle speech toward Pharaoh; this is a concrete enactment of making interaction easy for the other, and its hoped-for result is remembrance or fear.
terra: God answers Moses and Aaron's fear with إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ, placing divine accompaniment inside the feared mission for which Moses requested ease.

luna: This says whoever turns away from God's reminder will have a constricted life (مَعِيشَةً ضَنكًا). The section links Quranic remembrance with facilitation; this is a specific adverse outcome at the point of turning away from remembrance.
terra: God says He sent down a book فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ; revelation itself carries the addressees' remembrance or honor, joining the section's raised name to the Quran made easy for dhikr.
terra: God answers Noah's earlier call and saves him and his household from the great anguish, a concise direct formulation of relief from constriction.

luna: Job calls on God when harm has touched him, appealing to God's mercy. This gives the section's hardship-and-ease image another prophet's specific plea from within affliction. | terra: Job names the harm that has touched him while addressing the Most Merciful, giving a concrete afflicted speaker whose difficulty remains present in the prayer.

luna: God answers Job and removes the harm that had touched him. This is the distinct relief in the scene begun in 21:83, paralleling the section's claim that trial is met by easing. | terra: God answers Job, removes his harm, and gives back his family with as many again; one affliction is answered by doubled gift, a close thematic counterpart to one hardship and more than one ease.

luna: This recalls Dhun-Nun's appeal from the darkness after he departed in anger, when he thought God would not constrain him. It is another prophet's specific plea from distress, alongside the section's examples of Moses asking for his affair to be made easy. | terra: Jonah calls from layered darkness that there is no god but God and that he has wronged himself, staging remembrance from inside distress rather than after it.

luna: God answers Jonah, rescues him from anguish, and says He likewise rescues the believers. This ayah contributes the deliverance that follows the distress in 21:87. | terra: God answers Jonah and saves him from anguish, then says He likewise saves believers; the ayah turns one rescue into a continuing promise of relief.
terra: God's complete knowledge and prior record of heaven and earth are إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ, locating ease in divine mastery over an immense matter.

luna: This states that God has placed no hardship in the religion (مِنْ حَرَجٍ). It gives the section's ease-over-hardship theme as a general religious boundary, rather than as the two conditions' simultaneous presence. | terra: وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ makes absence of religious constriction a general divine act and pairs it with holding fast to God as protector.
terra: God charges no soul beyond its capacity and has a truthful record, presenting measured obligation as a standing divine rule rather than a single concession.
terra: وَتَحْسَبُونَهُ هَيِّنًا وَهُوَ عِندَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ makes “light/trivial” the speakers' false estimate of slander; it sharply limits the dictionary equation of easy with insignificant.
terra: The sky splits with cloud and angels descend, furnishing the event that 25:26 calls a hard day for unbelievers.

luna: This calls the Day of final sovereignty hard for the disbelievers (عَسِيرًا), a direct reversal of ease on a day of judgment. | terra: The day when true sovereignty belongs to the Merciful is عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ عَسِيرًا, locating hardness in the hearer's relation to judgment.
terra: ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَاهُ إِلَيْنَا قَبْضًا يَسِيرًا describes the shadow's easy or gentle withdrawal, a physical instance of ease as a light, smoothly executed action.
terra: When the two groups see each other at the sea, Moses says إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ; guidance is asserted within apparent entrapment before the path opens.
terra: Abraham asks for a truthful mention among later generations, supplying the prayer-side counterpart to God's act of raising a servant's name.
terra: The revelation comes in a clear Arabic tongue; the ayah supplies the intelligible linguistic form through which being eased on the Prophet's tongue reaches hearers.
terra: The origination and repetition of creation are إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ, showing that what appears resistant to creatures is ready for God.
terra: Those who strive for God are promised guidance into His paths, and God is with those who do good; exertion, an opened way, and divine company occur in one formulation.
terra: Re-creating creatures is described as easier for God, another Quranic use that grounds apparent impossibility in divine power rather than calling the result insignificant.
terra: The cancellation of the fearful hypocrites' deeds is وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا, using the root for decisive divine action rather than a pleasant human experience.
terra: A doubled punishment is وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا; the verse directly blocks “easy” from being heard as small or lenient punishment.
terra: Every lengthened or shortened life is in a record and إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ, presenting exhaustive measure as easy for God.
terra: God saves Noah and his household مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيمِ, giving the hardship-to-rescue half of a passage that then raises his mention.
terra: God leaves something for Noah among later generations; 37:79 supplies its content, so this ayah contributes the enduring raised-mention act after rescue.
terra: سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٍ فِي الْعَالَمِينَ states the lasting honorable mention left after Noah's rescue in 37:76, directly joining removed distress and elevated name.
terra: God saves Moses, Aaron, and their people from the great anguish, another exact rescue formulation concerning the same Moses who asks for ease elsewhere.
terra: God leaves something for Moses and Aaron among later generations; 37:120 names that lasting mention, following their rescue from great anguish.
terra: سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ gives Moses and Aaron an enduring honorable mention after 37:115's deliverance, again binding relief and raised remembrance.
terra: Job says that suffering and torment have touched him, introducing the resistant bodily hardship answered immediately in the next ayah.
terra: Job is told to strike with his foot and finds a cool washing place and drink; the commanded movement opens bodily ease inside the affliction of 38:41.
terra: God restores Job's family and as many with them as mercy and reminder, again placing a doubled gift after one named suffering.
terra: خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ gives a Quranic dual-hand expression directed to one act; it may echo the source's two hands at one work, though the ayah itself does not speak of ease or hardship.
terra: An opened breast receiving light is set against hearts hardened from God's remembrance; this binds expansion, hardness, and dhikr in one explicit contrast.
terra: قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ presents the Quran as free of crookedness so that people may fear God, the precise nonlexical reverse of difficulty defined as bending and entanglement.

luna: The section's dictionary note (not this ayah's wording) gives ع س ر the secondary sense of an ill-fated day. This recounts the wind sent against Aad during ill-omened days (أَيَّامٍ نَّحِسَاتٍ), a matching scene of calamity. | terra: أَيَّامٍ نَّحِسَاتٍ calls the wind-punishment days ill-omened, giving a Quranic scene for the source dictionary's secondary “unlucky day” sense of difficulty.

terra: The imagined non-Arabic Quran prompts an objection about its signs and language, while the actual revelation is guidance and healing; it clarifies why ease on the Prophet's tongue matters to hearers.
terra: وَإِنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ makes the Quran a remembrance or honor for the Prophet and his people, directly bridging elevated mention and facilitated revelation.
terra: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكَ repeats the tongue image and states remembrance as its purpose, a direct unquoted counterpart to 19:97.

luna: This gives the blind, lame, and sick exemption from blame in the campaign setting. It repeats the concrete pattern of accommodation for illness and bodily limitation that the section invokes through the fasting concession. | terra: The blind, lame, and sick bear no blame for exemption from fighting, a concrete bodily-capacity application of divine ease in obligation.
terra: The earth splitting as people emerge swiftly for gathering is حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ, an easy divine gathering on the very day other ayat call hard for unbelievers.
terra: فَالْجَارِيَاتِ يُسْرًا pictures effortless, smoothly prepared motion; it gives a physical Quranic instance of the source gloss “made smooth and ready.”

luna: This describes the dead coming from graves with humbled eyes like scattered locusts, the scene that leads directly into the disbelievers calling the Day hard in 54:8. Its own contribution is the terrifying emergence that frames their words. | terra: People emerge from the graves with humbled eyes like scattered locusts; this supplies the bodily scene whose unbelieving speech in 54:8 calls the day hard.

luna: As people hurry toward the caller on the Day of Resurrection, the disbelievers call it a hard day (يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ). The same hard-day wording makes this a pointed reversal of the section's assurance. | terra: هَذَا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ is the unbelievers' own recognition as they rush from the graves toward the caller, another exact Quranic “hard day.”

luna: After the account of Noah's people, the ayah says God made the Quran easy for remembrance (يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ). This is the same explicit Quran-and-dhikr connection named in the section. | terra: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ directly joins divine facilitation of the Quran to remembrance, one of the section's concluding claims.

luna: The section's dictionary note (not this verse's wording) extends ع س ر to an ill-omened day. This verse calls the day of the storm sent against Aad (يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُّسْتَمِرٍّ), a specific Quranic scene matching that secondary sense. | terra: فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُّسْتَمِرٍّ names the day of ʿĀd's violent wind an enduring day of ill omen, another direct scene for that dictionary sense.

luna: The storm scene continues from the ill-omened day in 54:19: the wind leaves Aad like uprooted palm trunks. This gives the calamity behind the section's secondary dictionary sense of an ill-omened day.
luna: After the storm image in 54:20, this asks how severe God's warning and punishment were. It completes the specific calamity that makes 54:19's ill-omened day more than a bare label.

luna: After the warning about Aad, this repeats that the Quran was made easy for remembrance (يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ), carrying the section's Quran-and-dhikr link into another warning. | terra: The repeated يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ returns after the account of ʿĀd, setting an accessible reminder beside an account of severe punishment.

luna: After the account of Thamud, this repeats the formula that the Quran was made easy for remembrance (يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ), another direct instance of the section's claim. | terra: The same Quran-for-remembrance refrain returns after Thamud, making facilitation a repeated opening within the surah's hard warnings.

luna: After the account of Lot's people, this again says the Quran was made easy for remembrance (يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ), extending the same repeated link named in the section. | terra: The fourth يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ repeats the promise after Lot's people and confirms that this ease is meant to produce remembrance.
terra: Calamity is written before it occurs and إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ; human hardship and divine ease occupy the same event from different standpoints.

luna: The helpers prefer the emigrants over themselves even in privation (خَصَاصَةٌ) and are praised for being protected from miserliness (شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ). This is a specific charitable response under hardship, set against the miserly path in 92:10.
terra: After deniers reject resurrection, God says raising and informing them of their deeds is وَذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ, opposing perceived impossibility with divine ease.
terra: Believers are told to fear God as much as they are able, listen, obey, and spend; capacity directly measures the moral demand while giving remains the path's positive act.

luna: In the divorce rulings, this promises a way out (مَخْرَجًا) for whoever is mindful of God. The section presents ease as a path; this is a specific opening out of a constrained affair, in the same legal passage as 65:4. | terra: Whoever fears God receives مَخْرَجًا, a way out; this opens the same passage as 65:4 and 65:7 and makes ease a path emerging from constriction.
terra: God provides from where the person could not reckon and is sufficient for one who trusts Him, specifying the hidden provision that accompanies 65:2's exit and 65:4's ease.

luna: In the divorce waiting-period rulings, this promises that God will make ease in the affair of whoever is mindful of Him (يُسْرًا). The section also presents ease as a way made ready for the God-fearing. | terra: وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْرًا makes ease in one's affair a divine gift tied to caution, closely joining 92:5-7 and 65:7.

terra: وَإِن تَعَاسَرْتُمْ names reciprocal difficulty over nursing arrangements, while the verse requires housing, support, payment, and consultation—the social opposite of making matters easy for another.

luna: The section explicitly sets its wording for ease “with” hardship against this promise of ease after hardship (بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا). The same roots are present, while the timing changes. | terra: بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا places ease after hardship; the section explicitly sets this sequence against 94:5's مَعَ, clarifying that Quranic relief can be subsequent as well as co-present.
terra: God makes the earth manageable and commands people to walk its paths and eat His provision, a physical instance of terrain made fit and ready for movement.

luna: The section's dictionary note sets al-yusrā and al-usrā as opposed hand terms and imagines both hands on one body; here a person receives his record in his right hand (بِيَمِينِهِ), marking one side of a sharply divided outcome.

luna: The opposite recipient in the same scene receives his record in his left hand (بِشِمَالِهِ), setting a contrary fate against 69:19. This makes the section's opposed hand-labels a concrete boundary between outcomes.
terra: God makes the earth an expanse for people, supplying the prepared ground whose purpose is stated as path-travel in 71:20.
terra: The prepared earth lets people travel broad ways, a concrete nonlexical parallel to ease staged as an opened, traversable path.
terra: قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا sets the demanding night practice in a limited quantity; 73:20 later translates that measured burden into “what is easy” of Quran.
terra: نِّصْفَهُ أَوِ انقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا makes the amount adjustable downward, a concrete link to the section's secondary sense of يَسِير as little.
terra: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ allows a measured increase and commands deliberate recitation, completing the adjustable practice later eased in 73:20.
terra: إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا calls revelation a heavy word, while 73:20 makes its recited amount easy; the same Quran can be weighty in charge and accommodated in practice.
terra: A day that makes children gray is set before the same surah's accommodated Quran reading in 73:20; the passage holds an unbearably hard day beside a practicable present duty.

luna: After describing night prayer and the limits of what people can sustain, this commands them to recite what is easy for them of the Quran (مَا تَيَسَّرَ). It is a concrete easing of worship that matches the section's reading practice. | terra: فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ makes the practicable portion of Quran the measure after God acknowledges illness, travel, fighting, and inability to keep the earlier night measure.
terra: فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِي النَّاقُورِ supplies the trumpet event that makes 74:9's “hard day” a concrete eschatological scene.
terra: يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ realizes the source dictionary's “hard day” as the day opened by the trumpet blast.

luna: The preceding ayah calls the Day hard; this adds that it will not be easy for the disbelievers (غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ). The repeated ease-root marks the opposite fate from the section's assurance. | terra: غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ continues 74:9 by denying ease specifically to the unbelievers, joining the two antonyms across adjacent ayat.
terra: The Prophet is told not to move his tongue hurriedly with the revelation, directly supplying the tongue and human strain presupposed by the claim that the Quran is eased on his tongue.
terra: God assumes responsibility for collecting the revelation and its recitation, identifying the divine action that makes the Prophet's reception possible.
terra: When God has recited it, the Prophet is told to follow its recitation; his task is made a responsive path rather than anxious self-production.
terra: God also assumes responsibility for explaining the revelation, completing the sequence of divine collection, recitation, and clarification behind its facilitated delivery.
terra: The righteous fear يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا قَمْطَرِيرًا, a nonlexical depiction of the grim hard day that the section traces through عَسِير.
terra: Those who love the immediate life leave behind them يَوْمًا ثَقِيلًا; the “heavy day” is a nonlexical counterimage to the source's easy as light.

luna: The section's root note glosses تيسّر as becoming easy and prepared; this ayah says God made the way easy for the human being (السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ). The way's precise referent may be birth or life, so the shared image is bodily facilitation rather than necessarily a moral route. | terra: ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ explicitly stages ease as a way God makes traversable for the human being.

luna: This introduces the person given his record in his right hand (بِيَمِينِهِ); 84:8 calls his reckoning easy. The hand itself is this row's link to the section's paired-hand image. | terra: Receiving the record in the right hand is the concrete event whose consequence 84:8 names an easy account.

luna: The section imagines ease and hardship through paired hands; 84:7 gives one person his record in his right hand, and this ayah says he will receive an easy reckoning (حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا). The verse itself joins ease to the right-hand scene. | terra: فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا makes ease the quality of the believer's reckoning, an eschatological counterpart to the hard day.
luna: After the easy reckoning in 84:8, this says the person returns to his people rejoicing (مَسْرُورًا). It supplies the relieving result of that easy outcome.

luna: The other recipient is given his record behind his back (وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ) and calls for destruction. This turns the right-hand/easy-account scene in 84:7–8 into a concrete opposite outcome. | terra: Receiving the record behind the back begins the opposite branch from 84:7-8's easy account, so the ease is shown as a discriminating outcome rather than a universal one.
terra: سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلَا تَنسَىٰ promises that God will make the Prophet receive and retain recitation just before promising to prepare him for ease in 87:8.

luna: Addressing the Prophet, God says He will facilitate him toward al-yusrā (لِلْيُسْرَىٰ), directly joining the section's ease-root to its path image. | terra: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ addresses the Prophet with the promise that God will prepare him for the easiest way, directly matching the section's speaker and path image.
terra: فَذَكِّرْ إِن نَّفَعَتِ الذِّكْرَىٰ turns the preparation for ease in 87:8 into the Prophet's work of reminding.
terra: سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰ identifies the fearing person as the one who receives that reminder, paralleling the cautious giver prepared for ease in 92.
terra: The most wretched person avoids the reminder, reversing 87:10's fearful hearer and showing the rejected side of the remembrance joined to ease in 87:8.

luna: The section frames ease and hardship as diverging paths; this says the human being did not break through the steep pass (الْعَقَبَةَ). It names a hard route, then 90:12–16 specifies acts that make the image concrete. | terra: فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ calls the morally saving way a steep ascent; it limits any reading of 92's prepared easy way as requiring no strenuous act.
luna: This asks what the steep pass introduced in 90:11 is. Its role is to open the sequence of demanding acts that contrasts with an easy path.

luna: The first act in the pass is freeing a person. It connects the section's path opened for the giver with a specific generous act that the neighboring passage calls difficult to accomplish. | terra: فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ defines the steep ascent through freeing a person, a costly giving act that nonetheless aligns with the giver led to ease in 92.

luna: The pass includes feeding someone on a day of famine (يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ). This brings hardship and giving into the same scene, while 90:11 frames the generous act as a steep route. | terra: إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ places feeding inside a day of hunger, a precise scene of beneficial action and hardship occurring together.

luna: The person fed in the steep-pass sequence may be an orphan who is a relative. This specifies whom the difficult act of giving reaches, complementing the giver's path in 92:7. | terra: The orphan of kin is one recipient of that feeding, specifying the generosity that belongs to the difficult ascent and the path of ease.

luna: The sequence also names a poor person in the dust. This is another specific recipient of the giving that the section associates with a path made easy. | terra: أَوْ مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ adds the destitute person in dust, keeping the act of ease toward another inside severe need.
terra: Mutual counsel to patience and mercy completes the steep path; endurance and mercy explain how moral ease coexists with exertion.
terra: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَاتَّقَىٰ supplies giving and caution as the human acts to which 92:7's prepared easy path responds.
terra: وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَىٰ adds affirmation of the best promise as the second condition completed by the ease of 92:7.

luna: For the one who gives and is mindful of God, God promises to facilitate the way toward al-yusrā (لِلْيُسْرَىٰ). This is the section's clearest parallel for ease as a divinely prepared path. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ makes ease a divinely prepared destination for the giver who fears God, exactly the moral path developed in the section.

luna: This names the miserly self-sufficiency that the section gives as the setup for the hard path; 92:10 supplies that destination. This ayah contributes the first trait that turns the person away from the easy path. | terra: بَخِلَ وَاسْتَغْنَىٰ identifies withholding and imagined self-sufficiency as the posture that issues in 92:10's hard destination.

luna: This says the person denies the best (وَكَذَّبَ بِالْحُسْنَىٰ), another part of the section's stated setup for the hard path; 92:10 then names that destination. Its contribution is the denial preceding the outcome. | terra: وَكَذَّبَ بِالْحُسْنَىٰ completes the reversal of 92:6 and explains why “facilitation” in 92:10 leads toward hardship.

luna: For the miser who deems himself self-sufficient and denies the good, God promises to facilitate the way toward al-usrā (لِلْعُسْرَىٰ). This is the stated opposite of the easy path in 92:7 and the section's joined pair. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ deliberately uses facilitation for the hard destination; it is the section's sharpest boundary against treating every facilitated path as saving ease.
terra: وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ shows that the self-sufficiency of 92:8 cannot rescue its owner when the hard path reaches its fall.
terra: إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ places guidance under divine care immediately after the paired easy and hard destinations, reinforcing that these are paths, not mere moods.
terra: مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ reassures the same Prophet that present silence does not mean abandonment, a stance of consolation continuous with 94's promise in difficulty.
terra: وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ الْأُولَىٰ promises a better later condition; its temporal sequence complements and contrasts with 94:5's simultaneous مَعَ.
terra: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ promises future giving and satisfaction to the same addressee, another form of divinely prepared relief.
terra: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَآوَىٰ recalls shelter within the Prophet's earlier vulnerability, like 94:1-4's past favors serving as evidence for promised ease.
terra: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدَىٰ recalls guidance out of being without a way, supporting the section's image of ease as an opened path.
terra: وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلًا فَأَغْنَىٰ recalls sufficiency following need, another past divine act grounding reassurance to the Prophet.
